During the period from the beginning of 2018 to the end of 2024, the position of Minister of Planning underwent significant structural changes. Most notably, the ministry was **abolished** for four years (2019–2022) under the Bolsonaro administration and folded into the "super" Ministry of Economy, before being recreated in 2023.

Here are the individuals who held the office during this timeframe:

### 1. Dyogo Henrique de Oliveira (2016 – April 7, 2018)
*   **Administration:** Michel Temer
*   **Status at start of 2018:** He was the incumbent at the start of the year. He left the cabinet in April 2018 to take over the presidency of the BNDES (National Bank for Economic and Social Development).

### 2. Esteves Colnago (April 10, 2018 – December 31, 2018)
*   **Administration:** Michel Temer
*   **Role:** He served as the final Minister of Planning, Budget, and Management before the ministry's temporary dissolution.

---

### **Interregnum: Ministry of Economy (2019 – 2022)**
On January 1, 2019, President Jair Bolsonaro merged the Ministry of Planning, the Ministry of Finance, and the Ministry of Industry into a single **Ministry of Economy**. 
*   **Minister of Economy:** **Paulo Guedes**
    *   During this period, Paulo Guedes held the legal powers previously assigned to the Minister of Planning. Technical planning duties were handled by various special secretaries within his department.

---

### 3. Simone Tebet (January 1, 2023 – Present)
*   **Administration:** Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
*   **Role:** Upon taking office, President Lula recreated the **Ministry of Planning and Budget (MPO)**. 
*   **Status:** Simone Tebet was appointed as the minister on the first day of the administration and remains in the position as of late 2024.

The **Ministry of Education** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação*), commonly known as **MEC**, originates from its previous name, the **Ministry of Education and Culture** (Portuguese: *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*), is a [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Brazil "Cabinet of Brazil")-level [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") [ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_federal_institutions_of_Brazil "List of federal institutions of Brazil") of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federative_Republic_of_Brazil "Federative Republic of Brazil").

## History of the institution

Before 1930, matters related to education were the responsibility of the *National Department of Education* ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Departamento Nacional do Ensino*), which was part of the [Ministry of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Justice_and_Public_Security_(Brazil) "Ministry of Justice and Public Security (Brazil)") at the time.

In 1930, as [Getúlio Vargas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get%C3%BAlio_Vargas "Getúlio Vargas") took office as [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Brazil "President of Brazil"), the **Ministry of Education and Public Health** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Saúde Pública*) was established, taking away education matters from the Ministry of Justice.

In 1953, the ministry was split into two: the [Ministry of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Brazil) "Ministry of Health (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education and Culture** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e Cultura*, with the acronym *MEC*, which lasts to this day).

In 1985, during [José Sarney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Sarney "José Sarney")'s presidency, it was again split into two: the [Ministry of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture_(Brazil) "Ministry of Culture (Brazil)"), and the **Ministry of Education**.

In 1992, as [Itamar Franco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Franco "Itamar Franco") took office as president, sports were made part of the ministry again, which was subsequently renamed **Ministry of Education and Sports** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): *Ministério da Educação e do Desporto*).

In 1995, during [Fernando Henrique Cardoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Henrique_Cardoso "Fernando Henrique Cardoso")'s presidency, that was once again changed, separating the **Ministry of Education** from the then [Ministry of Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Sports_(Brazil) "Ministry of Sports (Brazil)").

The incumbent Education Minister is senator [Camilo Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camilo_Santana "Camilo Santana").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_(Brazil)#cite_note-3)
